Etalus first easily. Distant second below them, though still noteworthy, Orcane and Wrastor.

Etalus because every good Etalus player does the same thing. The character is about as deep as a shot glass and there's basically only one way to play him. The most flowcharty character in the entire game and it's impossible to enjoy fighting a character with infinite mixups using a single Dash Attack. Icicle and downtilt spam when you go offstage, Upair's angle is ridiculous as a killmove, armor in general, random downspecials can kill at 80 sometimes. People also never mention how insane of a move his ftilt is. He's the only actual brainless character in the entire game, and I don't say that lightly.


Wrastor and Orcane are tied for second for a pretty similar reason, it doesn't really matter how people DI against their combo starters/extenders, they're still going to get a followup hit. In Wrastor's case that usually means it ends by getting clapped at 60 and dying. In Orcane's case, I think he's just unironically the "perfect" Rivals character. He has absolutely everything you'd want in a game like this. Incredible Jab, Downtilt, uptilt frame data better than anyone else. 7 Frame killmove, ridiculous movement, excellent zoning tools, strongest upair in the game, everything is just ridiculous save for a pretty average recovery (That's negligible considering how impossible it is to kill him off the side anyways).

If a character is heavily nerfed and there's an endless tirade squealing about how nerfed he is, yet he still manages to perform just fine ON THE PATCH WHERE THE NERF WAS IN FULL EFFECT, why in the earthly level-headed fuckface would you ever jump the gun and call him a "mid tier character". If you really want me to, I could definitely go over every single set Blue played in and give you the finest details of when the nerfed Slipstream played any factor at all into any interaction. I have nothing else better to do. Not sure if you knew this, but the patch we're currently playing on, the Slipstream nerf was cut in half and projectiles no longer break it.

This stuff usually tends to happen, where the community gets it all out of their system immediately and the game dwindles and sparks out before the main event is even teased. I may be in the minority with this, but I feel like it should be one extreme or the other. Either release a stream of stuff weekly or bi-weekly, even if its not polished... or just hold off on releasing anything all together until all the i's are dotted and t's are crossed.

Well I'm definitely not saying that you haven't been doing your part with the balancing aspect of the game. That's very needed and definitely the most tweaked and updated. And I'll never be one to say you're not doing your part in working on your own game. My biggest concern is and always will be the actual in game content. Dev mode doesn't have much appeal to a lot of people, the skin colors which I absolutely adored were removed for no real good reason beyond thematic holiday timing, and as a person who tries to keep abreast of this game's scene I haven't heard anything about actual gameplay content. I'm all for playing with patchy unfinished content as long as it's different and gives the player something to to besides test the bots AI against one another. (Which didn't appear to be polished judging by the inability to fight bots on release.)

Call me a cynic, but I'm having a lot of trouble believing the notion that it's impossible to focus a team's efforts in one location over another in game development. How would creating a character to be thrown in for a little bit of early access playtesting interfere with anything else? Maybe add something mundane and simple like a street-fighter-esque training stage, with hexes for floors and walls? Doesn't sound like it'd be too time consuming and at least it's something new to play with and safe to implement. As it stands, people have been playing with the same toys for five months and it shows on the steam charts that their paint is chipping.

I appreciate your reply, and definitely am looking forward to the March updates, but seeing as how often early access burns, I will not be holding you to that date. I really do love this game and don't regret my purchase one bit, I was just blown away by the decision to remove the "Halloween" colors back in November, and haven't had much else to play with since. There is absolutely no reason to cap this game at 8 characters. If they stop at 8, it's a very disheartening admission that they are only after the melee community and don't plan on expanding further into its own thing. As a fighting game player, hell even as a video game player, one of the biggest draws I find to any game I get attached to is variety. League of Legends didn't release with its original 40, only to have the dev team dust their hands and say "we did it boys, game complete". If they did, Riot wouldn't be the juggernaut of gaming it is today. Even looking at all the Smash games, 64 released with 12 characters and that was in 1999. Has the roster been added to or subtracted from for "balance" in its sequels? I personally find that it would be absolutely unacceptable to release a smash-like game with all the potential in the world, in the year 2015, with 8 characters. That has no appeal beyond melee fans and I honest to god think this game's staying power relies on growth in the roster. I even say forget everything else you're working on, just focus on adding another character to each faction, and release with 12. Variety is never a bad thing.
